result.title: SpectralRoute: Adaptive Spectral Routing for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Hyperspectral Segmentation
result.summary: Open-vocabulary semantic segmentation enables the recognition of arbitrary categories through natural language descriptions and has recently been extended from natural images to remote sensing. However, existing approaches primarily focus on three-channel optical imagery or limited-band multispectral data, while pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) struggle to directly exploit the rich spectral information of hyperspectral imagery (HSI) without additional adaptation. More importantly, different land-cover categories rely on distinct spectral cues, which may be weakened by uniform fusion. To address these challenges, we propose SpectralRoute, a training-free framework for open-vocabulary hyperspectral segmentation. Specifically, we construct complementary spectral views from HSI and enrich category descriptions with external spectral knowledge, enabling frozen vision-language models to extract diverse spectral-semantic responses. We then introduce a class-adaptive spectral routing mechanism that selectively amplifies discriminative spectral responses for each category, overcoming the limitations of uniform fusion. Furthermore, physical spectral priors are incorporated to refine predictions for visually similar land-cover categories. Experiments on three hyperspectral benchmarks demonstrate that SpectralRoute consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods without additional training.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SpectralRoute，一个免训练的高光谱开放词表分割框架：从高光谱构建互补光谱视图、用外部光谱知识扩充类别描述，并引入按类别自适应的光谱路由与物理先验来选择性放大判别性响应。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按类别选择性路由多路光谱证据、避免均匀融合」的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与多视图贡献分配提供线索；但该工作面向遥感分割、无 latent 推理状态与停止决策，路由是否仅依赖单次前向响应仍待核查。
